newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB drops fixed home loan rates.
newsitem.headline: FNB drops fixed home loan rates.

text.p: First National Bank (FNB) said on Friday it had dropped its fixed home loan rate to a minimum of 17.5 percent, effective from August 1.
The bank is the last of South Africa's big four banks -- Amalgamated Banks of South Africa, Standard Bank and Nedcor -- to cut its fixed home loan rates over the last month.
FNB said its decision to reduce its rates followed an assessment of the property and financial markets subsequent to the relaxation of exchange controls on July 1.

"The outflow of funds after the relaxation of exchange controls has not reached the anticipated levels and, after consideration of the many factors which impact on the property market we were able to make a realistic cut in the rate," FNB property finance division general manager Derek Price said.
The bank said borrowers could now fix their home loan rate at 17.75 percent over 12 to 23 months and 17.50 percent for 24 months.

"We are satisfied that these new rates -- the lowest on the market for 12 and 24 months at this time -- will make a measurable positive impact on the pocket of the average fixed rate borrower," Price said.

The revised rates are applicable to borrowers applying for new bonds and who opt for the fixed rate, those with existing fixed rates as they become eligible for renewal and existing bondholders who want to convert to the fixed rate option.
